steps.what: The harness picks tools over MCP and builds the context.
steps.breaks: Prompt injection hidden in a work order

steps.breaks: Frontier model used for every step

sections.title: Skills that compound
sections.subtitle: Click a card to flip: old way vs. AI way

skills.name: Test-driven development
skills.why: Tests become the spec an agent must satisfy.
skills.old: Write code, then tests, if time allows
skills.ai: Write failing tests first; let the agent turn them green; review the diff
skills.starter: Take one kata. Write the tests. Have an agent implement. Reject anything that edits your tests.

skills.name: Behavior-driven development
skills.why: Plain-language scenarios are a contract humans and agents both read.
skills.ai: Given/When/Then scenarios drive generation and gate acceptance
skills.starter: Write five scenarios for a feature you know. Generate the code. Run them as the gate.

skills.name: Chaos engineering
skills.why: Agents add new failure modes: model timeouts, tool errors, bad context.
skills.ai: Fault injection as a pipeline gate, including model and tool failures
skills.starter: Inject latency into one model call. Does your app degrade gracefully?

skills.name: Reliability engineering
skills.why: More change, faster. Stability must be designed, not hoped for.
skills.ai: SLOs for agents too; agents assist mitigation; you design the failure modes
skills.starter: Set an SLO and error budget for a project you already run.

skills.name: Security engineering
skills.why: Prompt injection, tool abuse and agent identity are new attack surface.
skills.ai: Secure by design, by default, in operations, for every agent
skills.starter: Threat-model one agent app: what can it read, call and change?

skills.name: Cost engineering
skills.why: Tokens and GPUs make cost a design property.
skills.old: Finance reads the bill next month
skills.ai: Track cost per successful outcome; route routine work to cheaper models
skills.starter: Log tokens and cost per task. Find your most expensive easy task.

skills.name: Performance engineering
skills.why: Latency now spans retrieval, models, tools and devices.
skills.old: Tune the query, add a cache
skills.ai: Latency budgets per hop; choose model size and location deliberately
skills.starter: Measure p95 latency for each step of one AI feature.

skills.name: Evaluation engineering
skills.why: Non-deterministic output needs measured quality, not a green checkmark.
skills.ai: Evaluators, golden datasets, quality gates in CI/CD, live evaluation
skills.starter: Build a 50-case golden set for one prompt. Re-run it on every change.

skills.name: AI red teaming
skills.why: If you don't attack your agent, someone else will.
skills.ai: Automated adversarial probes; track attack success rate
skills.starter: Point PyRIT at your own chatbot. Fix the first thing that breaks.

skills.name: Context & harness engineering
skills.why: What the model sees decides what the model does.
skills.ai: Design tools, context windows, memory and guardrails; connect over MCP
skills.starter: Wrap one tool you use daily as an MCP server.

skills.name: Edge & device engineering
skills.why: Intelligence is moving to plants, vehicles and laptops.
skills.ai: Hub-and-edge design; on-device models with GPU/NPU; offline operation
skills.starter: Run a model locally with Foundry Local. Compare latency with a cloud call.

skills.name: Containment engineering
skills.why: An agent can't be its own security authority.
skills.old: Run scripts with the user's full access
skills.ai: Policy-bound execution containers for generated code, tools and whole agents
skills.starter: Run a generated script in MXC. Use Learning Mode to draft a least-privilege policy.

skills.name: Verification & judgment
skills.why: The scarcest skill is knowing when the output is wrong.
skills.ai: Verify, integrate, steward; keep your own confidence earned
skills.starter: For one week, write down every AI answer you had to correct, and why.
skills.source: Lee et al., Microsoft Research, CHI 2025

sections.title: Patterns I keep seeing
sections.note: Generalized from customer work. No customer, figure or detail identifies anyone.

stories.title: AI with guardrails
stories.challenge: Teams want agents. Regulators want control and evidence.
stories.move: Policy as code, private networking, evaluation gates before production.

stories.title: Governed sandboxes
stories.challenge: Engineers need safe places to experiment. Requests were slow and manual.
stories.move: Sandboxes created from code, with policy, expiry and cost caps built in.
stories.lesson: Make the safe path the fast path.

stories.title: Compliance by design
stories.challenge: Every change must be traceable and validated.
stories.move: Requirements → scenarios → tests → release, with evidence produced by the pipeline.
stories.lesson: Audit evidence is a build artifact.

stories.title: Multi-region scale
stories.challenge: One platform, many regions, different latency and cost limits.
stories.move: Region strategy as architecture; failover drills; cost per region tracked.
stories.lesson: Where it runs is an engineering decision.
